pdf_title: PROPERTY STOLEN AND RECOVERED BY CATEGORY OF OFFENCES Property worth Rs. 3613.97 lakhs was stolen in 1970 in 4,86.608 cases and the recovery was of the value of Rs. 799.76 lakhs indicating a percentage of property recovered to property stolen of '22.1. The highest loss of property of Rs. 2402.20 lakhs was in 'House-Breaking' and 'Thefts' in as many as 4,33,326 cases. The percentage of recovery was very low in cases of 'Criminal Breach of Trust' and 'Dacoity', being only 9.7% and 11.3% respectively. Table XXI presents the statistics of property stolen and recovered by different categories of offences during 1970. The highest amount of property stolen was noticed in Uttar Pradesh (Rs. 1038.8 lakhs) approximately 28% of the total value of property stolen in the entire country. The highest percentage of property recovered to value of property stolen was recorded in Haryana (62.5%), followed by Tamil Nadu (58.4%), Jammu & Kashmir (58.2%), and Rajasthan (53.3%). Among the Union Territories, Delhi recorded the highest amount of property stolen viz. Rs. 186.2 lakhs and the recovery was also quite high viz. 42.4%. Among the cities, the highest amount of property lost/recovered was in the city of Bombay Rs. 195.7 lakhs and the least in Madras (11.8 lakhs) and the percentage of recovery in all these cities was about 40 on an average. The relevant detailed statistics for the different States, Union Territories and Cities are presented in Appendices XXV to XXX

notes: 148 policemen laid down their lives while on duty in 1970 as against 96 during 1969. The highest number of deaths of policemen was in the State of West Bengal (54), followed by Uttar Pradesh (25). 12 policemen were killed in Jammu and Kashmir and 30 in Maharashtra. These four States together accounted for about 2/3rd of the policemen killed in the entire country. ‘Riotous mobs’ and dacoity operations accounted for about 16% of total police casualties in the country. Accidents accounted for the deaths of 61 policemen, while criminals were responsible for the deaths of 33 policemen.

4,003 policemen were injured during 1970 out of whom 2,773 i.e. 69% were injured at the hands of ‘Riotous mobs’. The highest number of injuries took place in West Bengal (792). followed by Maharashtra (594) and Mysore (505) and in both these States most of them were injured at the hands of riotous mobs. In Rajasthan, criminals were responsible for the injuries of 152 out of 311 policemen injured in the whole State. Similarly, in Gujarat also, 110 policemen out of 153 policemen received injuries at the hands of criminals. Among the cities, Calcutta (354) and Bombay (227) recorded the largest numbers of policemen injured. Very few casualties are noticed in the Union Territories, except Delhi which recorded 69 policemen injured. The detailed statistics are exhibited in Table XXIII.
